case: Inquiry into tax benefits granted for Montenegro's house in Espinho
type: criminal inquiry (inquérito) on an anonymous complaint concerning Montenegro as the beneficiary; no one made a formal suspect (arguido)
description: An anonymous complaint alleged that Montenegro, then PSD leader, had signed a false statement to obtain the reduced VAT rate and the municipal property-tax (IMI) exemption for the rehabilitation works on the building where he lives in Espinho, and questioned the municipality's licensing. On 29 December 2023 the Prosecutor General's Office confirmed to DN that an inquiry directed by the Porto regional prosecution department (DIAP Regional do Porto) existed, was under judicial secrecy and had no formal suspects. Montenegro said he had received no special treatment, had done nothing ethically or legally inappropriate and welcomed the inquiry as a chance to close the matter.
outcome: Closed (arquivado) by the Porto DIAP, as announced on 2 December 2024. The prosecution service found that the works qualified as the rehabilitation of a building in an urban rehabilitation area, that the tax benefits rested on the administrative recognition of that status and did not exceed what the law provides, and that there was no indication that the municipality had favoured him or of unlawful interference in the licensing decision.
court: Ministério Público – DIAP Regional do Porto (Procuradoria-Geral Regional do Porto)
presumption_note: No one was made a formal suspect and the inquiry was closed without charges in December 2024. Montenegro is presumed innocent and denied any wrongdoing.
key_facts: Inquiry confirmed on 29 December 2023: under judicial secrecy, no arguidos
Closure announced on 2 December 2024 by the Porto prosecution service

case: Preventive inquiry (averiguação preventiva) concerning Luís Montenegro and Spinumviva
type: preventive inquiry by the prosecution service, in which Montenegro was the person concerned (visado); no criminal proceedings opened
description: On 12 March 2025, the day after his government fell, the Central Department of Investigation and Prosecution (DCIAP) opened a preventive inquiry in which Montenegro was the person concerned. According to the DCIAP, its scope was limited to media reports reproduced in complaints alleging that payments to Spinumviva, of which Montenegro had been a partner and which remained in his family, continued while he was Prime Minister without being owed, because the company could no longer have his professional services or because the fees exceeded market rates; such facts could, 'even if only to a small extent', ground suspicion of a risk of the crime of undue receipt or offer of advantage (Article 16 of Law 34/87). New complaints about the family's purchase of two flats in Lisbon were added. The DCIAP collected information from land and commercial registries, the data-protection authority, the Constitutional Court, the company, its clients and Montenegro, who also gave a statement; Montenegro said his and his family's bank statements had been examined.
outcome: Closed by a reasoned order of 16 December 2025, announced on 17 December: the DCIAP found no indication of the crime in question, no risk that it was occurring and no indication of any other crime, so the inquiry was not converted into a criminal investigation. A separate complaint by former MEP Ana Gomes, sent to the European Public Prosecutor's Office, was closed by that office on 27 November 2025 (RTP). In 2025 the prosecution service also opened and closed, as a 'lapse', a duplicate inquiry registered from an e-mailed complaint (RTP). Montenegro said the preventive inquiry had been 'in practice a genuine criminal inquiry'.
court: Ministério Público – Departamento Central de Investigação e Ação Penal (DCIAP); European Public Prosecutor's Office (Ana Gomes complaint)
presumption_note: A preventive inquiry is not a criminal prosecution: Montenegro was never a formal suspect (arguido) or charged, and the inquiry was closed in December 2025 for lack of any indication of a crime. He is presumed innocent and has denied any undue advantage.
key_facts: Opened 12 March 2025; closed 16 December 2025 (DCIAP note of 17 December 2025)
Possible offence examined: undue receipt or offer of advantage (Article 16, Law 34/87)
The two Lisbon flat purchases were added to its scope
European Public Prosecutor's Office closed the Ana Gomes complaint on 27 November 2025

case: Montenegro v. Entidade para a Transparência: appeal to the Constitutional Court over the Spinumviva client list
type: appeal (recurso) to the Constitutional Court against a decision of the Entidade para a Transparência (Montenegro as appellant)
description: Montenegro appealed to the Constitutional Court against an EpT decision of 4 April 2025 that required the clients of Spinumviva to be included in the register of interests in his single declaration. He argued that his administrative complaint to the EpT, decided on 28 May 2025, had suspended the deadline for going to court.
outcome: The Court refused to hear the appeal because it was filed on 2 June 2025, 'well after' the 15-day deadline, informing him on 21 January 2026 and confirming this on 19 February 2026. On 12 March 2026 the plenary unanimously rejected his complaint that the decision was null (he alleged a 'surprise decision' and the unconstitutionality of the Court's reading of the deadline), holding that the suspension of deadlines by optional administrative complaints applies only to the administrative courts. The decision is final: the client list must be included in his register of interests. The Court's ruling concerned admissibility and deadlines, not the merits of his objection.
presumption_note: This was an administrative-constitutional dispute in which Montenegro was the appellant; it involved no accusation of a crime against him.
key_facts: Appeal filed 2 June 2025 against the EpT decision of 4 April 2025
Rulings of 21 January, 19 February and 12 March 2026 (plenary, unanimous)
The EpT suspended decisions on analogous cases while this one was pending

case: Montenegro v. Entidade para a Transparência: pending appeals of 12 August 2025 and 20 May 2026
type: appeals (recursos) to the Constitutional Court against EpT decisions (Montenegro as appellant)
description: Montenegro filed appeals to the Constitutional Court on 12 August 2025 and 20 May 2026 against EpT decisions on Spinumviva; according to Correio da Manhã (via Observador), one of them seeks to prevent public access to the services the company provided to its clients and to the balances of bank accounts. The Court said the two appeals concern substantially the same matters. The Prime Minister's office denied filing 'new appeals', describing the May 2026 filing as an adaptation of the August 2025 case to a new EpT decision, and said the Court had not ruled on the merits.
outcome: Pending. As of 26 August 2026 the Constitutional Court confirmed there was still no decision on either appeal (Correio da Manhã via CNN Portugal); until it rules, public access to the elements concerned remains suspended. No later decision was found as of October 2026.
presumption_note: Montenegro is the appellant in an administrative dispute over the publication of parts of his declarations; no accusation of a crime is involved.
key_facts: The EpT's opposition procedure has suspensive effect on public access
